researcher_notes: OPUS REDO PASS — FINAL BATCH. Two remaining VisionNav documents: (1) '1657089341.pdf', an 18-page English full-range product catalog ('AUTOMATE YOUR INTRALOGISTICS Catalog / Full Range of Autonomous Industrial Vehicles and Smart System') documenting SEVEN model series (T/L/SLIM/P/E/R/Q) across 17 distinct spec blocks; (2) '1685356775.pdf', a 14-page image-only VNST20 Pallet Jack flyer (Copyright 2023) read via pdftoppm page images. Written to a SEPARATE file from docs/research_findings_opus_20260808_visionnav.json (which covers the individual single-model sheets) so the two document generations stay independently reviewable. GENERATION: this catalog is the older generation — model codes carry -01/-07 suffixes and (V)/(VL)/(VM) navigation-package markers. Decoding the marker (confirmed from the 'Positioning Method' row on each page): (V) = 'Vision-based Navigation'; (VL) = 'Vision-based Navigation+3D Laser Navigation'; (VM) = 'Vision-based Navigation+Magnetic'. This decode is itself a finding — the (VM) tow tractors are the only models in the whole VisionNav range that are NOT infrastructure-free, and the suffix is the only place the document says so. MAJOR STRUCTURAL PROBLEM — MODEL-CODE COLLISION: the catalog prints the SAME model code on physically different machines. 'VNR16(V)-07' appears twice (p.14 'Manual Handheld': 4500 kg dead weight, 6300 mm lift, 2442 mm long; p.16 'Manual Seated': 3910 kg, 7000 mm lift, 3229 mm long) and 'VNR25(V)-07' appears twice (p.15 'Standing Tiller': 4162 kg, 6500 mm lift; p.16 'Manual Seated': 5238 kg, 5500 mm lift). The ONLY disambiguator is the operator-station subtitle in the page header. I have used that subtitle in product_name and flagged it — a naming convention ruling is needed before import. AISLE-WIDTH CONVENTION: every forklift page prints TWO aisle figures, 'Min. Stacking Aisle Width' and 'Min. Turning Aisle Width'. I mapped min_aisle_width to the STACKING figure (larger, and the aisle that actually governs a stacking truck's working aisle); the turning figure is recorded in notes for every product. This matches the stored DB convention — VNSL14 holds 2250, which is exactly this catalog's stacking figure (its turning figure is 1600). For the R series, which prints stacking width both 'Gantry Retracts' and 'Gantry Extends', I used the EXTENDED figure on domain grounds: stacking physically happens with the gantry extended. Both figures are in field_sources for every R-series entry. UNIT CONVERSION APPLIED: 'Maximum Climbing Ability' is printed in DEGREES on every page but AP0's max_gradient unit is '%'; all values converted as tan(deg)*100 and both figures recorded. No other unit mismatches — the catalog is metric-first with imperial in brackets. DELIBERATELY NOT POPULATED on the Q-series tow tractors: max_payload. Page 17 prints 'Rated Load Capacity (Q) 4000kg / 6000kg' but the same table prints 'Fork Dimensions /', 'Fork Lift Height (h3) /' and 'Center Height of Traction Pin 324mm' — this is a pure tow tractor with no load deck, so the figure is a TRACTION rating and belongs in towing_capacity only. This is direct confirmation of the VNQ50/VNKQ20 pattern flagged last session, and it strengthens the suspicion that the DB's VNQ50.max_payload = 5000 is the same mis-file. Flagged, not corrected.
